references.text: Isaac's eyes were dim with age so that he could not see, in a similar way to how Israel's (Jacob's) eyes were heavy with age.
Isaac asked Jacob to come near and kissed him, just as Jacob now brings Joseph's sons near to himself, kisses them, and embraces them before blessing them.
Laban embraces and kisses Jacob when they meet, mirroring how Jacob kisses and embraces his grandchildren.
Joseph falls on Benjamin's neck and kisses all his brothers—a parallel to the kissing and embracing within the family.
Eli's eyes began to grow dim so that he could not see, a parallel to Jacob's weakened sight in old age.
A parallel between two prophetic figures (Jacob and Ahijah) who receive or give revelation despite physical blindness.
